messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: High tail latency for tenant KestrelSys (dedicated VPC pool vpc-us-west-2). Paging #eng-oncall. Incident severity: P2. Link: https://redwood.ops/incidents/INC-2026-0423

maria: acked. i'm on it. seeing alerts for queue depth and evicted requests. starting triage.

kevin: on my way. any customer reports? tenant-support, FYI.

tenant-support: support has an open ticket from KestrelSys — reports of slow responses since ~07:10 PDT. they saw intermittent 504s when performing multi-turn chat.

maria: quick telemetry: scheduler queue depth spiked to ~18k for the tenant, active workers at 100% gpu_util. tail_p95 latency > 2.8s for generate calls. overall cluster has spare capacity but this dedicated pool is saturated.

jon: logs from router show a lot of small token requests but high concurrency (many concurrent short-chat sessions). looks like batching knob is growing large because of high concurrency + long batching window.

maria: running live metrics query:

```
# prometheus-ish pseudo
sum(rate(redwood_scheduler_queue_depth{tenant="kestrelsys"}[1m])) = 18200
max(redwood_gpu_utilization{pool="vpc-us-west-2"}) = 98
p95(redwood_request_latency_ms{tenant="kestrelsys"}) = 2840
```

kevin: hypothesis: max_batch_tokens is too high for the short requests which causes batch build-up and longer head-of-line latency. suggested quick mitigation: reduce max_batch_tokens and max_batch_size for tenant override + lower max_wait_ms to force earlier dispatch.

maria: agree. let's do a tenant-scoped change (no global rollout). canary to 3% of traffic then 100% for the tenant only. we need an action plan and approval from oncall.

kevin: plan:
1) apply scheduler override for tenant kestrelsys:
```
PATCH /admin/tenants/kestrelsys/scheduler
{
  "overrides": {
    "max_batch_tokens": 2048,
    "max_batch_size": 8,
    "max_wait_ms": 25,
    "enable_backpressure": true
  },
  "canary": 0.03
}
```
2) monitor latency & queue depth 2min
3) if p95 drops < 800ms and queue depth drops, scale to 100% for tenant
4) notify tenant-support to tell customer we are doing a config tweak

maria: approved. kevin, you have the keys.

kevin: executing now.

sre-bot: deploy triggered by kevin at 1826789230. Job ID: deploy-7721

kevin: applied canary=3% at 1826789240. will watch.

maria: initial impact: canary shards show p95 760ms, queue depth on those shards down to ~1.2k. global tenant queue still high because only 3%.

jon: looks good on canary. no errors in deploy logs. recommend widen to 100% for tenant.

kevin: widening to 100% now.

sre-bot: deploy widen executed at 1826789345. Job ID: deploy-7721-widen

maria: post-widen metrics 1826789400:
- tenant queue depth: 2.1k -> 700
- p95 latency: 2840 -> 610ms
- gpu_util: 98% -> 85%
- error rate: 504s dropped from 1.8% -> 0.2%

tenant-support: pinged KestrelSys's primary contact. they confirm noticeable improvement.

kevin: note: throughput has decreased ~12% due to smaller batches; cost per token up slightly but customer-facing latency wins. we should track for billing and ops.

maria: next steps:
- keep override active for 2 hours and monitor auto-scaling behavior
- open follow-up to evaluate longer-term scheduler tuning and prefix caching improvements for this tenant
- run a regression evaluation on cost vs latency for KestrelSys

devops: would it make sense to add a bespoke tenant quota throttle so queues can't grow past N? we can enforce soft backpressure at the ingress.

kevin: yes probably. short term, we've stabilized. long term, we should add ingress backpressure + KV prefix caching + per-tenant concurrency caps.

maria: handoff: i'm handing the incident to kevin for monitoring window. if anything regresses, page eng-oncall.

kevin: taking over monitoring. will escalate to platform if queue re-appears or autoscaler fails to respond.

sre-bot: incident state change: mitigated at 1826789500 by kevin. severity de-escalated to P3.

tenant-support: KestrelSys asks for a follow-up call to discuss permanent tuning and SLA implications. scheduled with their SE for 16:00 PDT.

maria: notes for runbook:
- cause: tenant-specific workload pattern (high-concurrency short requests) + scheduler knobs sized for long-running batches => head-of-line latency.
- mitigation: tenant scheduler override (max_batch_tokens=2048, max_batch_size=8, max_wait_ms=25)
- tradeoffs: increased unit cost, slightly lower throughput. recommended additional mitigations: KV prefix caching, ingress concurrency cap, tenant-specific autoscaling thresholds.

jon: adding a small patch to the config API so support can trigger tenant overrides with proper RBAC and audit logs.

kevin: monitoring window in progress. last check 1826790350: stable. will close after 2h cold-watch.

maria: thanks team. great quick coordination. :thumbsup:

kevin: closing handoff note: I'll file the incident report and link perf graphs.

sre-bot: incident resolved (mitigated) at 1826790450. follow-up ticket created: TICKET-5821
